_comment: Reconstruction thresholds for canonical/mir @ 5ce58e5f (C++/CMake Wayland compositor). Ground truth: .workshop/dev.yaml (ubuntu@26.04; vscode-remote + copilot + project-mir; system tunnel plug localhost:8000; actions cmake/build/package/test/doc/ccache) plus .workshop/mir/ (desktop + gpu + build/ccache mount plugs, doc tunnel slot 8000, setup-base installing build-dep, setup-project running cmake).
_derivable_from: CMakeLists.txt (ptest target), debian/control Build-Depends, HACKING.md (ccache + mold + cmake flags), doc/CMakeLists.txt (doc-html/doc-run targets), doc/sphinx/Makefile (SPHINX_PORT ?= 8000, sphinx-autobuild), doc/sphinx/conf.py (http://127.0.0.1:8000), .github/workflows (ubuntu-26.04, resolute).
_base_note: CI pins ubuntu-26.04/resolute, but the skill's canonical default is 24.04 and either is defensible from the tree; the report records which was picked.
_sdk_note: No Store SDK is derivable: vscode-remote and copilot are maintainer conveniences, not toolchain evidence. The C++ toolchain has to come from an in-project SDK.
_desktop_note: Gated from 2026-08-13: the repo IS a Wayland compositor and its debian/control build-deps (libwayland-dev, libdrm-dev, libgbm-dev, libegl1-mesa-dev, libgles2-mesa-dev, libinput-dev, libxcb-*) are unambiguous in-tree evidence that the developer needs to RUN what they built, not only compile it. Both models missed this in the first round; toolchain-signals.md now carries the signal.
_interfaces_note: Advisory, not gated. The maintainers give the build tree and ccache mount plugs and take a gpu plug; HACKING.md evidences ccache in-tree, but choosing mount over an in-tree build dir is still a judgement call, so it is recorded and discussed rather than failed.
